title: TAPPaaS Zone Field Definitions
description: Defines the structure and valid values for zone definitions in zones.json

Management.description: TAPPaaS nodes and self-management zone. Must be locked down with no access from other zones or the Internet. Typically only one zone named 'mgmt'.

WAN.description: ISP hand-off segment shared by the WAN modem and every node's 'wan' bridge NIC, so the HA firewall VM keeps its uplink after failing over to another node. Switch-internal only: always state=Manual with a VLAN tag, which keeps it out of every trunk (vmnet_all_active_tags) and stops zone-manager creating an interface or DHCP server — the ISP modem is the sole DHCP server on the segment. See zones.json 'wan'.

Service.description: Zone where service modules live. Multiple service zones can exist to serve different user bases (e.g., separate business units or home/business separation).

Client.description: Zone for client devices. Multiple client zones can exist for different user populations.

IoT.description: Zone for IoT devices. Typically multiple zones for different types of (often insecure) devices.

Guest.description: Security zone for unauthorized or guest clients.

DMZ.description: Demilitarized zone for services that need controlled exposure.

Overlay.description: Non-VLAN overlay network (e.g. NetBird/WireGuard) whose peers carry their own source CIDR (e.g. 100.64.0.0/10). Has no interface, DHCP or firewall rules — always state=Manual with vlantag=0. Exists so consumers like network:proxy access-list.sh can resolve the overlay CIDR. See zones.json 'netbird' (issue #367).

type.changeNote: A zone's type fixes its tier band and its whole rule posture. Changing it is a different zone: delete and re-add.

state.description: The activation state of the zone in a TAPPaaS instance

Active.description: Zone is created and configured by zone-manager (VLANs, DHCP)

Mandatory.description: Same as Active; zone must exist and cannot be disabled

Inactive.description: Zone is not created; if it exists it will be removed by zone-manager

Manual.description: Zone is managed manually; zone-manager will neither create nor remove it

state.changeNote: Has its own verbs with the transition guards: `network-manager enable|disable|manual <zone>`. Leaving 'Mandatory' needs --force there, which a generic --set would bypass.

typeId.description: Unique number identifying the zone type category
typeId.note: Should match the typeId from the 'type' field
typeId.changeNote: The numeric type band. Paired with subId to derive the VLAN tag; not re-decidable in place.

subId.description: Unique number (0-99) identifying the zone within its type category

vlantag.description: Unique VLAN tag for the zone
vlantag.changeNote: The VLAN a zone IS. Changing it would strand every guest currently tagged into it — each one needs re-tagging and a new lease. Delete the zone and re-add it, moving its guests deliberately.

ip.description: IP range associated with the zone in CIDR notation
ip.changeNote: The zone's subnet. Every guest in it is addressed from here, so a change re-addresses all of them; that is a migration, not a field edit.

bridge.description: Network interface the zone is associated with. For a VLAN zone this is the physical trunk it rides. For a non-VLAN zone (vlantag 0 — Overlay/Manual) it is the OPNsense interface token its traffic arrives on, e.g. 'wireguard' for a WireGuard overlay; ADR-021 D3a needs it to place that overlay's caddy-reach rule
bridge.changeNote: The physical trunk the zone rides. A change moves the whole zone to different hardware.

access-to.description: List of zones this zone can connect to. zone-manager creates pass rules from it (unless --no-firewall-rules).

special_values.internet: Allows traffic to any destination (outbound internet access)
special_values.all: Creates a wildcard pass rule (destination: any)

access-to.note: Zone names (e.g., 'srv', 'dmz') allow traffic to that zone's network
access-to.changeNote: A zone-to-zone pass rule. Reconciling it rewrites firewall rules; nothing reboots and no address changes. This is the field #538 was raised about.

pinhole-allowed-from.description: List of zones that can have pinhole connections to specific ports in this zone. Used to validate module-specific firewall rules against zone policies.
pinhole-allowed-from.changeNote: Which zones may open port-specific pinholes into this one. Same cost as access-to: a rule swap.

snat-allowed-from.description: List of zones whose traffic into this zone may be source-NAT'd (masqueraded) to this zone's gateway address. The gate for network:snat: a module's snatFrom request is intersected with this list, and naming a zone outside it is refused, not trimmed. Absent or empty refuses every request, so masquerade is strictly opt-in per zone.
snat-allowed-from.note: Every zone here MUST already be able to reach this one (R1), by either mechanism: an access-to edge on the source zone, or an entry in this zone's pinhole-allowed-from. Masquerade without reachability is meaningless, and allowing it separately would make source NAT a second, weaker way into the zone. access-to:["all"] counts; "internet" does not, being reach out rather than into a zone. Enforced by 'snat-manager validate' — network-manager validate does not read this gate. Every device in this zone loses client attribution for masqueraded sessions — the device, and anything reading its logs, sees the gateway address instead of the real client — so this is a zone-wide consent, not a per-module one.
snat-allowed-from.changeNote: Which zones may be masqueraded into this one. Same cost as pinhole-allowed-from: a rule swap. Removing a zone here strands any module still requesting it — the next network:snat reconcile refuses the request and removes the live rule.

tier.description: Trust rank in the ADR-014 strict lattice (0 = most trusted). Governs the direction of 'access-to': an edge may only run downward. Authored (stamped by the archetype), never derived — it records declared security intent so a zone configured against its intent can be caught. Absent on the types listed in 'tier_exempt_types'.
tier.note: Tier 5 is reserved for the 'internet' boundary token and is never authored on a real zone. See 'tier_model' and 'invariants.I1' below.
tier.changeNote: Trust rank in the ADR-014 lattice. Changing it re-derives which access-to edges are legal, so a reconcile may DROP edges the new tier forbids. Reported by validate before it is applied.

isolated.description: Inbound quarantine flag. An isolated zone accepts NO zone-wide 'access-to' from anyone (the 'mgmt' control-plane exception aside); inbound reach is granted exclusively per-module via 'pinhole-allowed-from'. Orthogonal to 'tier' — iotCams (tier 6) and iotUntrust (tier 3) are both isolated.
isolated.note: This is the ADR-007 isolation invariant expressed as a field rather than prose. Enforced by 'invariants.I2'.
isolated.changeNote: Inbound quarantine. Turning it on withdraws every zone-wide pass INTO this zone at the next reconcile — disruptive to traffic, but not to any guest, and instantly reversible.

serves.description: The ENVIRONMENT whose service zone this Client or IoT zone consumes. A symbolic reference resolved on every reconcile against config/environments/<env>.json '.network.zone' — so it survives the install-time 'srv' -> '<defaultEnvironment>' rename that strands literal service-zone names (issue #424).
serves.note: Authored once via 'network-manager bind <zone> --environment <env>'. Resolution ADDS the environment's service zone to this zone's effective 'access-to', and adds this zone to that service zone's effective 'pinhole-allowed-from'. An isolated zone contributes ONLY the pinhole direction, never an inbound 'access-to' (R2 is preserved). The derived edges are rendered into zones.effective.json and are NEVER written back into zones.json, which stays purely authored.
serves.changeNote: Has its own verb: `network-manager bind <zone> --environment <env>` (or --unbind). bind resolves the environment first, so a typo fails at the command rather than three reconciles later (ADR-014 D2).

DHCP-start.description: Starting offset for DHCP range within the subnet
DHCP-start.changeNote: The DHCP pool's low offset. Narrowing a pool below its live leases does not evict anyone; existing leases run to expiry.

DHCP-end.description: Ending offset for DHCP range within the subnet

tftp-server-name.description: DHCP option 66 (tftp-server-name / next-server). IP or hostname of the TFTP/PXE server advertised to clients in this zone. When set, zone-manager configures both the BOOTP header (dnsmasq dhcp-boot next-server/sname) and an explicit dhcp-option 66 on the zone's DHCP scope. Must be set together with 'bootfile-name' — one without the other is not a usable boot configuration.
tftp-server-name.changeNote: DHCP option 66. Picked up by clients at their next lease renewal.

bootfile-name.description: DHCP option 67 (bootfile-name). Boot file handed to PXE clients in this zone (DHCP 'file' field), e.g. 'pxelinux.0' or 'ipxe.efi'. When set, zone-manager configures both the BOOTP header (dnsmasq dhcp-boot filename) and an explicit dhcp-option 67 on the zone's DHCP scope. Must be set together with 'tftp-server-name'.

description.description: Human-readable description of the zone's purpose
description.changeNote: Documentation only. Nothing on any plane depends on it.

tier_model.description: The ADR-014 strict trust lattice. 'access-to' is the coarse, zone-wide, DOWNWARD trust flow; everything that must go UPWARD is a narrow per-module pinhole. This replaces the descriptive tier prose that used to live in zones.json._README.tier_model, which could not be machine-checked because its own edges violated it.
tier_model.rule: R1 — for every edge 'A access-to B', tier(A) <= tier(B). Never upward.

5.name: Internet (boundary token)
5.note: Not a real zone — the rank of the literal 'internet' in access-to.

tier_exempt_types.description: Zone types that carry no 'tier' and are SKIPPED by the tier invariants I1, I3 and I4. Overlay zones are non-VLAN WireGuard segments with no meaningful trust rank (and 'admin' legitimately carries access-to: ['mgmt'], an upward edge into tier 0); WAN is the switch-internal ISP hand-off with no interface, DHCP or rules.

archetypes.description: The single source of tier-correct zone defaults. 'network-manager add <name> --archetype <A>' stamps type/typeId/tier/isolated and the access-to seed, then auto-allocates subId/vlantag/ip. Also the conformance target for invariant I4: every zone's (type, tier, isolated) triple must match one of these.

control.description: Control plane: hypervisors, backup, firewall, identity, cicd

trusted-client.description: Trusted end-user devices; reaches its service zone by pinhole

iot-cloud.description: Internet-dependent trusted IoT: appliances, media, monitoring

iot-local.description: Local-only IoT: no internet, automation devices

invariants.description: Machine-checkable security gates run by 'network-manager validate' (zones-check). Each is a WARNING by default and an error under --strict. They promote the old zones.json._README.pr_review_checklist from human review to code.

I1.name: Monotonic access-to
I1.rule: For every edge 'A access-to B': tier(A) <= tier(B). 'internet' counts as tier 5.
I1.exempt: The 'mgmt' control plane (tier 0) reaches every zone for operational visibility; zones whose type is in tier_exempt_types; any zone with no authored tier (reported as a note until back-filled).
I1.remedy: An upward edge must be expressed as a per-module pinhole instead — add the source to the target's pinhole-allowed-from and declare the specific IP/port rule in the module.

I2.name: Isolation floor
I2.rule: A zone with 'isolated': true must not appear in ANY zone's access-to.
I2.remedy: Grant reach per-module via the isolated zone's pinhole-allowed-from.

I3.name: Egress boundary
I3.rule: A tier-6 (no-egress) zone must not list 'internet' in its access-to.
I3.remedy: If the devices genuinely need internet, the zone is iot-cloud or iot-untrust (tier 3), not iot-local/iot-cams.

I4.name: Archetype conformance
I4.rule: Every zone's (type, tier, isolated) triple must match an entry in archetypes.catalog.
I4.exempt: Types in tier_exempt_types; any zone with no authored tier.
I4.remedy: Either correct the zone's fields to its declared intent, or create it with 'add --archetype <A>'.

I5.name: No zone-wide DMZ reach
I5.rule: No zone may list 'dmz' in its access-to (ADR-021 D3b, issue #618).
I5.why: An access-to edge compiles to <source subnet> -> <target subnet> on every port, and the DMZ gateway is the firewall itself (webgui.interfaces and ssh.interfaces are unset), so the edge hands the admin GUI (8443) and SSH (22) to every host in the source zone. The DMZ also holds workloads, which the edge reaches zone-wide.
I5.exempt: 'mgmt' only — the control plane keeps its full visibility list.
I5.remedy: Reaching the reverse proxy needs nothing: zone_manager emits a caddy-reach pass to the DMZ gateway /32 on tcp/80+443 for every candidate zone. Reaching a DMZ workload is a per-module pinhole via 'dmz'.pinhole-allowed-from.

zone_key.description: The key for each zone entry in zones.json
zone_key.note: camelCase only — no underscores or hyphens (#278). This is what network-manager authorZone() enforces; the schema previously allowed hyphens, which no code path would accept.
